Fit a GLMM to each response, choosing its error distribution

Source: R/fit.R
fit_responses.Rd

Fits, for every response, one generalised linear mixed model per candidate error distribution with glmmTMB::glmmTMB(), and keeps the one that fits the data best. The null models are not involved here: following the post-estimation approach, the model is chosen for the data and the null models are tested afterwards from its predictions (estimate_interactions()).

Usage

fit_responses(
  data,
  responses,
  design,
  families = NULL,
  response_types = NULL,
  trials = NULL,
  offset = NULL,
  time_structure = "interaction",
  dispersion = "common",
  random = NULL,
  control = NULL,
  residual_checks = TRUE,
  n_sim_residuals = 500L,
  seed = NULL,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

The data frame given to describe_design() (same treatment combinations; other columns may be added).

responses

Character vector with the names of one or more numeric response columns.

design

A must_design object from describe_design(). Designs with checks of severity "problem" are refused.

families

NULL (default) to choose the candidates from each response (see Details); a named list of family objects used for every response, e.g. list(gaussian = gaussian(), gamma_log = Gamma("log")); or a named list with one such list per response.

response_types

NULL (default) or a named character vector with "count" or "continuous" for some responses, to override the automatic detection used to choose the default candidates.

trials

NULL (default) or a character vector named after responses that count successes out of a known number of trials (survivors out of the animals added, emerged out of the eggs), giving the column with the number of trials of each observation, e.g. c(survivors = "n_start"). These responses are modelled as binomial or beta-binomial and their means are probabilities.

offset

NULL (default) or a character vector named after count responses giving the column with the sampling effort of each observation (volume filtered, area or time sampled), e.g. c(daphnia = "volume_l"). The model includes offset(log(effort)), only log-link candidates are used, and means are per unit of effort. Every value of the response needs an effort.

time_structure

How treatment effects relate to sampling time when the design has time: "interaction" (default; a separate mean for each treatment combination and time, no assumption of constant effects) or "additive" (treatment effects constant over time on the scale of the link function).

dispersion

Which observations share a dispersion (variance) parameter: "common" (default; one for all), "by" (one per by group) or "cell" (one per treatment combination and by group; the candidates with a dispersion parameter then need two or more units in every combination). Ignored for Poisson and binomial candidates, which have none.

random

NULL (default) adds a random intercept for each groups column of the design that can be estimated (see describe_design()) and one per experimental unit when some unit has more than one row (repeated measures or subsamples); "none" removes random effects; any other string is used as the random part of the formula in lme4 syntax, with column names of data, e.g. "(1 | tank) + (1 | block)". Custom terms can also use the internal columns .unit (the units), .time (the sampling times, as a factor) and .g_<name> (the groups of each groups column, made unique within by groups).

control

NULL (default) or the output of glmmTMB::glmmTMBControl(), passed to every fit. By default the iteration and evaluation limits of the optimiser grow with the number of fixed effects (see Details); the rest of the settings are those of glmmTMB.

residual_checks

If TRUE (default), simulation-based residual checks of the DHARMa package (uniformity, dispersion and zero inflation) decide which candidates may be selected. Needs DHARMa installed.

n_sim_residuals

Number of simulations for the residual checks. Default 500.

seed

NULL (default) or a whole number. The residual checks run with this seed through withr::with_seed(), which restores the random number state of the session afterwards. With NULL, a seed is drawn from the session's random number stream; either way it is stored in settings$seed, so the selection can be repeated exactly.

quiet

If FALSE (default), a message reports each response as it is fitted.

Value

An object of class must_fit, a list with:

  • fits: a list with one element per response, holding response, status ("ok" or "failed"), reason, model (the selected glmmTMB fit, by maximum likelihood), model_reml (the same model refitted by REML, used for the small-sample correction of estimate_interactions(); NULL if the refit failed), family (name of the selected candidate), link, response_type and type_source ("detected", "declared", "trials" or "families"), selection (data frame with one row per candidate: family, link, random (random part used), converged, aic, p_uniformity, p_dispersion, p_zero_inflation, n_tests_passed, residuals_ok, selected, message), checks_passed (TRUE, FALSE if no candidate passed all the residual checks, or NA if they were not run), formula (of the selected candidate), n_obs, n_missing (rows without a response value) and grid (treatment combinations and times predicted later).

  • design: the design.

  • settings: the arguments used, with the seed (and whether it was given), the families of the candidates given in families and the versions of must, R, glmmTMB and, with the residual checks, DHARMa.

Details

Model. Treatment combinations are coded as one factor (a cell-means model), so any design is handled: full or partial factorials, ray designs or a few combinations of many stressors. With time_structure = "interaction" the fixed part is one mean per treatment combination, time and by group; with "additive" it is one mean per treatment combination and by group plus a common effect of time.

Default candidates. Responses with trials are binomial: binomial and beta-binomial, both with a logit link. Otherwise whole non-negative numbers are treated as counts (the type_source says the type was detected): Poisson and negative binomial (NB2), both with a log link, but the Poisson is selected only if the negative binomial does not converge, as happens when the counts show no overdispersion to estimate. With overdispersed counts and four units per combination, the AIC chose the Poisson in a fifth of simulated experiments (the residual checks passed it too), and then the tests of estimate_interactions() rejected true null models too often; fitting the negative binomial kept them close to their nominal error, at a small cost in power when the counts are truly Poisson. Continuous values: Gaussian, Gaussian with log link, Gamma with log link and lognormal if all values are positive; Gaussian, Gaussian with log link and Tweedie if there are zeros; Gaussian only if there are negative values. With an offset only the log-link candidates are kept. Use response_types when the detection is wrong (a density rounded to whole numbers is not a count) and families for other distributions (e.g. glmmTMB::beta_family() for proportions without a number of trials, such as cover).

Optimiser. A cell-means model has one parameter per treatment combination (and time), which can be more than the default limits of the optimiser of glmmTMB (300 iterations, 400 evaluations) allow. By default they are raised to 20 iterations and 30 evaluations per fixed effect (never below glmmTMB's defaults); a fit that reaches them still counts as not converged.

Combinations with only zeros. On a log link, the mean of a treatment combination (at a time) whose values are all zero is on the boundary of the parameter space (minus infinity on the link scale); on a logit link the same happens when all values are zero or all are successes. For these candidates the mean of such a combination is fixed at that boundary (map of glmmTMB), so the rest of the model is estimated normally; their AIC counts the fixed parameters, so that it stays comparable with the identity-link candidates. With time_structure = "additive" only combinations with such values at every time are fixed (otherwise their mean is not on the boundary). estimate_interactions() tests the contrasts that involve these combinations from the probability of the observed zeros.

Random intercepts at zero. With few units, the variance of a random intercept is often estimated at zero, which often makes the Hessian singular. If that happens to an automatic random intercept (random = NULL), the candidate is refitted without it and the reduced model is kept when it reaches the same maximum likelihood, whether or not the full model converged; the random column of selection and the reason say so. Terms given in random are never removed.

Selection. Candidates that fail to converge or have a non-positive definite Hessian are discarded, and so is the default Poisson for counts when the negative binomial is left. With residual_checks = TRUE, a candidate passes when the three DHARMa tests give p >= 0.05; if at least one candidate passes, only those compete, and otherwise those passing the most tests (checks_passed = FALSE: inspect that model before using it). The candidate with the lowest AIC is selected. Candidates whose AIC differs by less than 1e-4 fit equally well: in a cell-means model without random effects the link does not change the fitted means. The log link is then preferred, because its means stay positive as the multiplicative and dominance null models need, unless some combination has only zeros, in which case the identity link is preferred; the reason says which.

REML refit. The selected model is refitted by restricted maximum likelihood (REML), whose variance estimates account for the number of fixed effects. estimate_interactions() uses it for its default small-sample correction; the selection itself uses the maximum-likelihood AIC.

Assumptions

  • A random intercept per unit implies the same correlation between any two samplings of a unit. Temporal autocorrelation is only modelled if a structure is given in random, e.g. random = "ar1(.time + 0 | .unit)" (first-order autoregressive; it treats the sampling times as equally spaced).

  • With dispersion = "common", all treatment combinations and by groups share one dispersion parameter on the scale of the family; with very different groups (species, populations), use "by" or "cell".

  • The selection among candidates is not accounted for in the uncertainty of later estimates.

Missing values and zeros

Rows with a missing response are left out for that response only and counted in n_missing. Zeros are kept as observed values and no transformation is applied (see "Combinations with only zeros").

References

Brooks, M. E., Kristensen, K., van Benthem, K. J., Magnusson, A., Berg, C. W., Nielsen, A., Skaug, H. J., Mächler, M., & Bolker, B. M. (2017). glmmTMB balances speed and flexibility among packages for zero-inflated generalized linear mixed modeling. The R Journal, 9(2), 378–400. doi:10.32614/RJ-2017-066

Madge Pimentel, I., et al. (2025). Hypothesis-driven research on multiple stressors: An analytical framework for stressor interactions. Ecology and Evolution, 15, e71959. doi:10.1002/ece3.71959

Examples

jars <- expand.grid(
  salinity = c("ambient", "high"),
  warming = c("no", "yes"),
  replicate = 1:5,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
jars$jar <- seq_len(nrow(jars))
# Algal counts: each stressor halves the expected count
mu <- 40 * ifelse(jars$salinity == "high", 0.5, 1) *
  ifelse(jars$warming == "yes", 0.5, 1)
jars$algae <- stats::qpois(c(0.2, 0.35, 0.5, 0.65, 0.8)[jars$replicate], mu)
# Survivors out of 20 animals per jar
jars$n_start <- 20
jars$survivors <- c(18, 15, 16, 9)[match(paste(jars$salinity, jars$warming),
  c("ambient no", "high no", "ambient yes", "high yes"))] +
  c(-1, 0, 1, 0, 0)[jars$replicate]
design <- describe_design(jars, c("salinity", "warming"),
  control = c(salinity = "ambient", warming = "no"), unit = "jar")
fits <- fit_responses(jars, c("algae", "survivors"), design,
  trials = c(survivors = "n_start"), residual_checks = FALSE, seed = 1,
  quiet = TRUE)
fits
#> <must_fit> 2 response(s); time structure: interaction; dispersion: common; random effects: none
#> Residual checks: not run; seed: 1
#>   algae: nbinom2 (log link; count, detected), AIC 114.2, n = 20, missing = 0, residual checks: not run
#>   survivors: binomial (logit link; binomial, trials), AIC 71.4, n = 20, missing = 0, residual checks: not run
fits$fits$algae$selection
#>    family link random converged      aic p_uniformity p_dispersion
#> 1 poisson  log   none      TRUE 112.2431           NA           NA
#> 2 nbinom2  log   none      TRUE 114.2431           NA           NA
#>   p_zero_inflation n_tests_passed residuals_ok selected message
#> 1               NA             NA           NA    FALSE        
#> 2               NA             NA           NA     TRUE
